ops.title: An abandoned shutdown stage parks the host alive holding its flock, so a supersede against a live daemon strands the incumbent until SIGKILL
ops.description:
Field-proven 2026-08-29 on yasyf-forge-studio, daemonkit v0.23.0 via captain-hook 12.22.3. A `deploy` Supersede against a live host could not complete:

    captain package: land delivered app: daemonkit: process did not provably exit
    context deadline exceeded

The host's own log, verbatim:

    2026/08/29 19:32:30 WARN daemonkit: shutdown stage failed err="child 54245: daemonkit: process did not provably exit (the settlement ladder timed out unproven; the record is left for the next generation)"
    2026/08/29 19:32:30 ERROR daemonkit: shutdown abandoned stages; retaining flock until stopped abandoned=1

Child 54245 was ALREADY DEAD — `ps` found nothing — while `daemon.records` still listed it live (`"live":[{"pid":54245,...,"comm":"python3.13"}]`).

THE STATE IS NOT THE BUG. The record self-heals: after a restart it read `{"cores":[]}{"live":[],"owner":{"pid":30166,...}}` with no intervention, exactly as "the record is left for the next generation" advertises, and `internal/proc/store.go:186-191` persists the whole value on every add rather than appending. So the ladder's contract is being honoured and nothing needs scrubbing. The wedge is in the OUTGOING PROCESS: it abandons the stage, keeps the flock, and never exits.

That is deliberate, not emergent — `serve.go:278-284` logs and then calls `park()`, documented at `:285-288` as holding the flock until one of `drainSignals = {SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP}` (`serve.go:140`) arrives. Nothing in the upgrade path sends one, so deploy's quiesce waits for an exit that will never happen. An intentional hold-for-an-operator state is unreachable by the tooling that must get past it, and is indistinguishable from a hang.

FIX THE ABANDON PATH, NOT THE PROOF PATH. Proving a vanished PID exited may be impossible in general — a PID that no longer exists is indistinguishable from one you failed to observe. What is fixable is what happens when the ladder gives up: abandoning a stage should not leave a live process holding an exclusive lock indefinitely. A bounded ladder that exits, surrendering the lock for the next generation to reclaim, turns a permanent wedge into a restart — and the evidence above shows that reclaim already works.

CALL PATH: child settlement times out and publishes `Reap == ReapUndetermined` (`control.go:58-60`) -> `own.go:317-320` turns that terminal into a fault -> `serve.go:278-284` abandons and parks. Note the fault message's "the settlement ladder timed out unproven" is inherited wording describing the CHILD's failure; on this branch the outer loop did not time out at all, and the string sent one reader down the wrong path.

PREDATES THIS INCIDENT: `grep -c 'shutdown abandoned'` on that host's log returns 8, including one on 2026-08-28.

BLAST RADIUS AND RECOVERY: a supersede against a live host can strand the incumbent — alive, socketless, flock held, helper down. The app bundle is NOT damaged (inode unchanged, no partial swap). Recovery is always exactly one force-restart: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/<host-label>`, plus a plain `launchctl kickstart gui/$(id -u)/<helper-label>` to bring the helper back. That restored the host fully, stale record cleared, in seconds.

First domino in the observed case was a hook worker dying on a TypeError (cc-notes bug dee57af), but the defect here is independent of what killed the child: any child whose exit cannot be proven reaches the same park.

ops.text: A shutdown that abandons a stage terminates and surrenders the flock, so the next generation reclaims it on restart instead of an operator sending SIGKILL
